knowledge.text: Returned programs must use the executor-bound INPUT_PATH/OUTPUT_PATH without reassigning them: a first-attempt top-level binding such as `INPUT_PATH = INPUT_PATH` is rejected before execution with the format error 'Only simple top-level literal path bindings may be adapted'. In two current pairs the Parent hit exactly this error on its first attempt (train:577-40, train:82-30) and recovered only after removing the rebinding, while the candidate programs in the same tasks used the bound names unmodified and executed on their first code attempt. This is consistent with the added clause that forbids defining, reassigning, or hardcoding the path names.

Prose narration or more than one fenced code block in the response is rejected with the format error 'Return exactly one complete python fenced block without surrounding text'. Two Parent attempts on train:47766 were rejected this way (one opened with an exploratory sentence and supplied two code blocks; another gave prose plus one block). Candidate-side format errors in the current batch were instead incomplete or truncated generations ('Model generation did not finish normally', e.g. train:47766, train:51090, train:398-14), so the added single-block/no-prose requirement targets the multi-block failure mode but did not eliminate all format-error loss.

Grading reads saved cell values with data_only=True and performs no recalculation, so a bare formula reads as empty. In the current pair train:57445 the Parent wrote a SUMIFS formula and injected XML cached results without a verified literal fallback and scored 0/4 (hard=0), whereas the candidate computed the lookup in Python and assigned literal values directly and scored 4/4 (hard=1). Formula cells carrying injected caches are still workable when handled correctly (Parent train:32255 12/12, train:10747 1/1, train:46121 48/48; candidate train:46121 48/48), so assigning literal computed values is the safer default, reserving formula-plus-verified-cache for tasks that explicitly require a formula.

The edit also instructed preserving pre-existing values and not stripping existing number formats or fills. In the one current pair with a formatting-heavy multi-sheet consolidation (train:398-14) both sides scored identically at 53/56 (hard=0) with the same three mismatched cells (COLLECTION!E9, COLLECTION!F5, COLLECTION!F8), so no measurable effect of this clause is observed on that task and the shared mistakes persisted on both sides.

The candidate returned an incorrect K40 (hard=0, 0/1) after building an embedded SUMIF/SUMIFS reconstruction and inferring the table's year axis from the existing formulas, using only 3 attempts and 2 executions. Because the edit jointly added formula-semantics reconstruction and a no-narration single-program workflow, the regression cannot be assigned to one clause; the pair shows that reconstructing an ambiguous row-versus-column year axis from existing formulas can overcomplicate a task that direct recomputation handles.

On train:82-30 (extract whole numbers from 'Raw Data' into a fixed grid matching the 'Manual Result' order), the Parent's submitted attempt scored 3/54 (hard=0) by emitting numbers row-by-row, while the candidate's first code attempt emitted them column-by-column and scored 54/54 (hard=1), matching the reference layout. On train:56274 both sides had to populate D9:D12 on 'Sheet2' from the month selected in D7; the Parent scored 0/4 (hard=0) while the candidate's first attempt scored 4/4 (hard=1). Both wrote literal values into the same four cells and neither visibly verified the output, so which change produced the difference is unresolved; the pair is retained as a supported Parent-failure/candidate-success asymmetry on identical answer cells.
